newsitem.title: USA: NorTel backs Q2, full year forecasts.
newsitem.headline: NorTel backs Q2, full year forecasts.

text.p: Northern Telecom Ltd President and Chief Operating Officer John Roth on Wednesday said he was comfortable with analysts' estimates of the company's earnings for the second quarter and the year.
"When you look at the analysts' composites, we are comfortable with that," Roth said at an analysts' conference in New York.

According to First Call, analysts on average expect the company to earn $0.57 per share in the second quarter, compared with $0.42 in the same period last year. For the year, earnings are expected to rise to $3.07 per share from $2.40.
Roth also said the company was aiming for revenue growth in the "mid-teens" for 1997.

That forecast excludes about three percentage points of growth expected to be generated by WilTel, a new venture formed through the combination of Northern Telecom's subsidiary that sells corporate telephone equipment with a Williams Communications Group subsidiary.
Nothern Telecom, based in Toronto, posted 1996 revenues of $12.8 billion. Last month, its chief executive, Jean Monty, said revenues should grow by between 15 percent and 20 percent in 1997.
Roth said the first quarter provided the company with good momentum for the year, as earnings rose by 28 percent and revenues by 29 percent, surpassing analysts' expectations.
"One quarter does not make a year but it is a nice start," he said.
